title: Journal of Emerging Investigators (JEI)
description: A student-focused research journal with scientist feedback and an educational peer-review process. A strong route for turning an original experiment into a carefully written paper; acceptance is not guaranteed and review cannot be expedited.
eligibility: Middle- and high-school authors aged 13+; initial submission before university enrollment. A senior adult mentor must coauthor, and an adult must submit on the student's behalf.
cost: $49 submission fee; limited need-based scholarships. Payment does not guarantee publication.
effort: Original research, manuscript template, adult mentorship, and revision after review.
lifecycleEvidence: Submission guidance is available; no calendar deadline verified. Manuscripts are handled in order received, with no expedited review. Confirm requirements before submitting.

title: National High School Journal of Science (NHSJS)
description: A high-school research journal publishing original studies and articles on developments in science and policy. Its stated review team includes graduate students, postdocs, and scientists. Read the formatting requirements before preparing a submission.
eligibility: Targeted toward high-school students and their original research. Match the journal's submission category and research ethics requirements.
cost: Free to read; author fees were not verified. Confirm all charges before submitting.
effort: Full manuscript and journal-specific citation/formatting requirements; revisions may be needed.
lifecycleEvidence: The journal invites submissions and provides a submission-form request. No fixed deadline or explicit year-round policy was verified.

title: Young Scientists Journal
description: A youth-run science journal accepting original research, review articles, and science writing. Research goes through student editorial review and an academic advisor; blog and magazine pieces are different formats, not equivalent research publications.
eligibility: Authors must be ages 12–20 at submission. International student community; use the author guide for your article type.
cost: Current author fees not verified; check before submitting.
effort: Chicago references, British English, and multiple review stages. The journal warns publication can take months.
lifecycleEvidence: Author instructions and submission link are published. No exact deadline or explicit rolling policy was verified.

title: Journal of Open Source Software (JOSS)
description: A professional, peer-reviewed journal for substantial open-source research software, with a citable DOI after acceptance. Relevant to mature simulation or scientific-computing tools—not a shortcut for a small class project or a notebook.
eligibility: Submitters must be major software contributors. Not a high-school-specific program; no school-level restriction is stated in the inspected requirements. Requires demonstrated research use and more than six months of public development history.
cost: Free to read and publish; no article-processing charge.
effort: Research impact, open-source license, public development, documentation, tests, releases, and a short software paper.
lifecycleEvidence: Submission instructions are available. No calendar deadline was verified; editors assess scope and software readiness before review.

title: arXiv — research preprints
description: Share a complete scientific manuscript publicly before or alongside journal review. arXiv is a moderated preprint repository, not peer-reviewed journal acceptance. Check a future venue's preprint and anonymity policies before posting.
eligibility: Registered authors submitting topical, refereeable scientific work. New authors or categories may require endorsement; not a high-school-specific publication program.
effort: A complete manuscript, appropriate category, distribution license, and possible endorsement/moderation.
lifecycleEvidence: Submissions follow a recurring announcement schedule, not an annual competition deadline. The daily processing cutoff is not a deadline for eligibility; review the submission guide.
